**Generated:** 2026-08-26T05:22:19.036Z · **Commit:** 028946fd · **Nodes:** 169

Zero-runtime-dependency Node.js harness that coordinates Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and Gemini-compatible agents through committed .agent state. Host rule or SessionStart hook -> shared BOARD/map/log context -> CLI and skill workflows -> verified task handoff. Project maps and skill evidence are Markdown/JSON files backed by Git; there is no database or application authentication layer.

**Stack:** JavaScript, Markdown, TOML, YAML, JSON

## Architecture

### Shared protocol and state

AGENTS.md and the committed .agent/ contract every host reads: board, thread, tasks, logs, map. The one canonical copy of each fact.

- `AGENTS.md` — Canonical always-on collaboration protocol for every host: inspect shared .agent state, claim file scopes before edits, and log verified outcomes at clock-out. The other host-specific rule files are generated from this one.
- `CLAUDE.md` — Generated Claude-facing copy of AGENTS.md. It carries the full shared-state and file-ownership protocol so Claude sessions receive it without relying on hooks alone; edit AGENTS.md and regenerate instead of changing this file.
- `.agents/rules/godkit.md` — Generated Antigravity-facing copy of the canonical AGENTS.md protocol. It is byte-for-byte rule content for a host with no hook enforcement, so changes belong in AGENTS.md and the sync generator.
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — Generated GitHub Copilot-facing copy of the canonical AGENTS.md collaboration rules. It exists as a host adapter and must be regenerated from AGENTS.md rather than edited independently.
- `templates/BOARD.md` — Canonical one-screen shared-state template for agent roster, exclusive file claims, active tasks, known bugs, binding decisions, and the three latest handoffs.
- `templates/MAP.md` — Initial placeholder project-map template that marks the map as not built and directs an agent to run the godkit-map workflow.
- `templates/task.md` — Per-task lifecycle template defining ownership, file scope, exit condition, phase, and structured Plan, Execute, Review, Test, and Handoff evidence sections.
- `templates/THREAD.md` — Append-only inter-agent message template for timestamped, attributed, task-linked actionable communication, including recipients and blockers.
- `templates/rules/cursor-header.md` — Cursor-rule frontmatter template that marks generated Godkit rules as always active with an empty glob filter and a shared-protocol description.
- `templates/gitattributes` — The -merge rules for the generated half of .agent/, shipped as a template because godkit init writes them into every project. They lived only in this repo's own .gitattributes, which npm does not ship, so init crashed from an installed package.
- `templates/log.md` — The session log skeleton. Its frontmatter scalars are quoted so a generated log parses under the stricter skill frontmatter reader.
- `README.md` — The public contract: install, compatibility, hooks, CLI, skills, project skills and evidence. Every claim here is asserted somewhere in tests/ — the compatibility table and the hook table are the two that drift first.

### Session runtime

lib/session.js, lib/work.js and lib/paths.js — per-session state under an owned root, session-scoped work evidence, and every bounded, symlink-refusing read of shared state.

- `lib/lazy.js` — Centralizes lazy-mode configuration, runtime state, host-specific hook output, and instruction loading. Runtime mode is stored in one host-wide .godkit-lazy-active file, so concurrent sessions currently share and overwrite the same state.
- `lib/session.js` — Host-neutral hook input and per-session runtime state. Session ids are hashed before they become path components and state lives only under a godkit-owned directory, so one session can never read or clear another. Also the atomic writer (temp + fsync + rename, optional compare-and-swap and .bak) that every config write in the package goes through.
- `lib/work.js` — Session-owned evidence that a tool changed project files — the thing clockout judges. Shell tools compare a before/after Git fingerprint that excludes .agent/, edit tools mark work only for successful paths outside it. A dirty working tree is deliberately NOT evidence: it says nothing about which session made it.
- `lib/paths.js` — Locating shared project state, and every bounded read of it. Hooks execute in the active worktree while .agent/ belongs to the MAIN worktree, so state survives linked-worktree removal and stays common to every agent. Reads below .agent/ reject symlinks and stop at a byte budget, so a project-controlled file cannot turn a session brief into a local-file reader.

### Hook enforcement

hooks/*.js. brief injects state at session start, work-track records what this session changed, clockout blocks the turn until its log exists, map-watch reports staleness. Generated registrations keep the plugin manifest and the settings installer in step.

- `hooks/work-track.js` — The lifecycle hook that feeds work evidence: pre captures a fingerprint, post compares, edit records a direct edit, end clears the session. Registered on PreToolUse, PostToolUse and SessionEnd — without it nothing records work and clockout can never fire.
- `hooks/clockout.js` — Stop hook. Blocks the turn when THIS session changed project files and has no log naming it, and keeps blocking until that log exists. Judges the session, not the directory: another agent's dirty file is not evidence about you, and a log naming a different session does not clock you out. stop_hook_active short-circuits, or a blocked turn would loop forever.
- `hooks/brief.js` — SessionStart hook. Injects a bounded, no-follow view of shared state — board, map freshness, project skills, newest logs, THREAD tail — under one total budget, so an arriving agent starts from the same truth without a project file being able to steer what it reads.
- `hooks/install.js` — Standalone hook registration for a settings file: a thin CLI over lib/install.js with --uninstall and --dry-run. Paths derive from where this file actually lives, so moving the package is a re-run rather than a text hunt.
- `hooks/lazy-activate.js` — SessionStart hook that resolves the godkit-lazy mode for this session and injects its ruleset. Mode state is per session, under the owned state root.
- `hooks/lazy-subagent.js` — SubagentStart hook. Inherits the parent session's lazy rules; a malformed matcher fails closed and warns rather than broadening its own scope.
- `hooks/lazy-mode-tracker.js` — UserPromptSubmit hook tracking /godkit-lazy switches and deactivation for the session.
- `hooks/map-watch.js` — PostToolUse (Bash) hook. After a command that lands a change, says whether the map went stale — and stays quiet otherwise, because a warning that fires constantly gets muted.
- `hooks/godkit-hooks.json` — The plugin hook manifest read by Claude Code and Codex. GENERATED from the HOOKS list in lib/install.js by scripts/sync-hooks.js; CI fails if it drifted. It was hand-maintained until a hook was added to the settings installer and not to this file.
- `hooks/godkit-hooks.json` — Ten registrations across SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop and SessionEnd. Matchers are chosen to mean the same under Claude Code (literal or regex) and Codex (always regex).

### Install and ownership

lib/install.js with hooks/install.js and scripts/uninstall.js. One definition of what godkit created, so nothing it did not create is ever replaced or removed.

- `gemini-extension.json` — Antigravity/Gemini extension manifest. It exposes the packaged skills and agents directories and selects AGENTS.md as the extension context file.
- `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — Claude plugin marketplace entry for the local godkit package, including owner metadata, description, category, and local source root.
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` — Claude Code plugin manifest. It publishes the godkit package identity and points Claude at the shared hook registry rather than duplicating hook definitions.
- `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` — Codex plugin manifest exposing the package's shared skills, agents, and hook registry. Keeping these as paths makes Codex consume the same canonical assets as the other hosts.
- `lib/install.js` — The single source of truth for what godkit installs and what it may remove. HOOKS lists every registration once; both the standalone settings installer and the generated plugin manifest derive from it. Ownership is the safety property: a destination is ours only if it is a link back into this package or a copy carrying our marker, and anything else is refused rather than replaced.
- `scripts/uninstall.js` — Removes what a host's own uninstall cannot see: installed skill directories, hook registrations, and the session-state root. Shares every ownership decision with lib/install.js, so what install created is exactly what uninstall removes — nothing else.

### CLI and map pipeline

bin/godkit.js over lib/scan.js, lib/batch.js, lib/graph.js, lib/freshness.js, lib/managed.js and lib/hotspots.js: scan, analyze, save, honest staleness, and the churn-and-blame ranking behind godkit refactor.

- `lib/scan.js` — Deterministic filesystem scanner that categorizes authored files, applies hard skips plus a documented subset of .agentignore/.gitignore, and regex-extracts resolvable relative imports. Unknown types and files over 400 KiB are intentionally absent from the map input.
- `lib/batch.js` — Greedy deterministic clusterer for semantic-analysis calls. It favors import-connected files, then same-directory neighbors, under a 60 KiB budget while guaranteeing every non-data file is placed once even when one file exceeds budget.
- `lib/graph.js` — Persistence and projection layer for project memory: guarded graph loading, portable path sanitization, node/edge normalization, saving, structural signatures, and generated MAP.md rendering. Node IDs are identity, duplicate nodes resolve last-wins, and dangling edges are dropped.
- `lib/managed.js` — A managed block is godkit's few lines inside a file the user also owns. init used to skip any host file that already existed, which silently meant "this project gets no rules"; overwriting would have eaten the user's text. Marked blocks do neither, and ambiguous or hand-edited markers are refused rather than guessed at.
- `lib/freshness.js` — Is the map still true? staleness() is git-only and safe on every session start; classify() decides how much to rebuild. It fails CLOSED: an unreadable status, a meta sha the repo no longer has, or a failed diff all report unknown or stale — never fresh. A hook that blesses a map nobody verified is the one wrong answer.
- `lib/hotspots.js` — Which code files the log stream says are hot: claimed in `scope:`, listed under `## Did`, or named as a root cause under `## Bugs`, cross-referenced against the map for fan-in. Reads no source code and scores no file the map does not know, so prose that merely looks like a path cannot rank. The deterministic half of godkit-refactor.
- `bin/godkit.js` — The CLI: init, install, hooks, scan, save, skills, evolve, refactor, doctor, uninstall. It owns no policy — ownership lives in lib/install.js, managed blocks in lib/managed.js, graph rules in lib/graph.js, rankings in lib/hotspots.js — so every command is a thin, testable shell over a library.

### Skills and evidence

skills/, agents/, commands/ and lib/evolve.js — the shipped procedures, plus project skills judged by owned snapshots and log-derived trust. godkit-evolve evolves those procedures; godkit-refactor evolves the source code from the same log stream.

- `agents/architect.md` — Prompt contract for the architecture synthesis pass after batch graphs are merged. It derives project metadata, 3-8 named layers, and a 5-9 step start-here tour without inventing framework or runtime claims.
- `agents/file-analyzer.md` — Prompt and schema contract for turning one scan batch into graph nodes and observed edges. It requires every assigned file to be read, stable relative-path IDs, actionable summaries, no guessed relationships, and exactly one scratch JSON output.
- `commands/godkit-doubt.toml` — Command adapter that forwards arguments to the godkit-doubt skill for pressure-testing a decision before it is recorded on the board.
- `commands/godkit-evolve.toml` — Command adapter that forwards arguments to godkit-evolve for capturing, deriving, or repairing project-owned skills under .agent/skills.
- `commands/godkit-execute.toml` — Command adapter that invokes the five-stage godkit-execute pipeline and passes through the requested plan or execution context.
- `commands/godkit-frontend.toml` — Command adapter for the godkit-frontend design-taste skill, forwarding UI context and arguments to its visual direction workflow.
- `commands/godkit-git.toml` — Command adapter for parallel-agent git mechanics, including worktrees, commit checkpoints, and shared .agent merges.
- `commands/godkit-handoff.toml` — Command adapter for clock-in, scope claiming, and evidence-bearing clock-out through the godkit-handoff skill.
- `commands/godkit-help.toml` — Argument-free command adapter that asks godkit-help to display the shared-state layout, ladders, skills, and CLI reference card.
- `commands/godkit-lazy.toml` — Command adapter that passes the requested lite, full, ultra, or off intensity to godkit-lazy, including mode switching and reporting.
- `commands/godkit-map.toml` — Command adapter that directs godkit-map to build or incrementally refresh graph.json and MAP.md with any caller-supplied scope.
- `commands/godkit-output-enforcement.toml` — Command adapter for locking deliverable counts and rejecting placeholder or truncated output through godkit-output-enforcement.

### Verification and release guards

tests/, scripts/sync-*.js, scripts/check-versions.js and the workflows. Generated files, agreeing manifests, a tag-only publish, and a packed-install smoke.

- `tests/freshness.test.js` — Unit tests for rebuild classification thresholds, top-level path normalization, human freshness summaries, and exclusion of .agent from staleness checks. They exercise classify directly but do not create git repositories to cover staleness command failures.
- `scripts/sync-rules.js` — Generates every host's always-on rule file from AGENTS.md, adding Cursor frontmatter only where required. --check turns the same projection into a CI drift detector.
- `tests/save.test.js` — CLI integration tests for graph save behavior, including graph/MAP/meta output, partial retention versus full replacement, corruption and missing-input refusal, tmp cleanup, path privacy, and freshness status.
- `scripts/sync-hooks.js` — Generates hooks/godkit-hooks.json from the HOOKS list in lib/install.js; --check fails if it drifted. A generated manifest cannot disagree with the installer, which is exactly how work-track came to be missing from one of them.
- `scripts/check-versions.js` — Every version-bearing manifest must carry the same version, and on a tag push that version must equal the tag. An empty or non-release tag now fails instead of skipping the check — the case where skipping is most dangerous.
- `package.json` — Zero runtime dependencies, Node 18+, bin godkit. `files` is the allowlist that decides what an installed package actually contains — a runtime file missing from it works in a checkout and 404s for everyone else, which the packed-install smoke test now catches. pretest runs the generated-file and version checks.
- `tests/runtime.test.js` — The hook runtime boundaries: shared state resolves to the main worktree from a linked one, reads stay inside .agent/ and inside a byte budget, session state is isolated and cleanable, work evidence tracks the session, lazy mode belongs to one session.
- `tests/cli.test.js` — What init and save do to files a user also owns, and what freshness reports when git cannot answer. Every case here is a silently-wrong failure: a rule file that never landed, a map node for a deleted file, a stale map reported as current.
- `tests/hook-install.test.js` — Install idempotence and the ownership rule. The two bugs it exists for: matching our entries by package name (which matched nothing, so re-runs appended), and filtering whole groups (which took a user hook out with ours).
- `tests/hooks.test.js` — Hooks never throw, never block a read-only session, and never loop. Clockout is asserted against recorded session work, not a dirty tree, and every hook runs against a temp CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR so no test writes real home config.
- `tests/package.test.js` — Contract tests: the package ships what the README promises, manifests agree, generated files are current, and — the one that catches an allowlist bug — the packed file set can actually run godkit init from a temp directory.
- `tests/evolve.test.js` — Project-skill snapshots, quarantine, frontmatter parsing, trust promotion and demotion, and fixture cleanup.

## Start here

1. **AGENTS.md — the protocol itself** — Two rules and the clock-in/clock-out checklist. Every other rule file in the repo is generated from this one, so this is the only copy worth reading.
2. **.agent/ — the shared state those rules operate on** — BOARD.md is claims, bugs and binding decisions; THREAD.md is the conversation; tasks/ and log/ are append-only. Read the templates to see the shape init writes.
3. **bin/godkit.js — every command, each a thin shell** — The dispatch table is the fastest index of what godkit does. No policy lives here; each command delegates to a library in lib/.
4. **lib/paths.js — the read boundary** — Every read of shared state goes through here: bounded, containment-checked, symlink-refusing. Read it before any code that touches .agent/, because it explains what those callers are allowed to do.
5. **hooks/brief.js and hooks/clockout.js — where the protocol is enforced** — brief injects the board and map at session start; clockout blocks the turn when a session that changed files wrote no log. On hosts without hooks the rule file is the only enforcement, which is why they say the same thing.
6. **lib/scan.js and lib/graph.js — the map, deterministic half** — Walk, categorize, resolve imports, batch; then normalize and save. saveGraph is load-patch-save and refuses to overwrite a graph it could not read, which is why one bad parse cannot reset the project memory.
7. **lib/evolve.js and lib/hotspots.js — two things derived from one log stream** — evolve ranks the procedures a project repeats; hotspots ranks the files it keeps breaking. Same evidence, different unit, and neither keeps a second store that could go stale.
8. **tests/package.test.js — the release contract** — What the package promises: the files allowlist, agreeing manifests, one command per skill, generated rules in sync, and a real pack-then-run-init. Read it to learn what is allowed to change.

## Recall

Grep `.agent/graph.json`, never load it whole: search `"name"`, `"summary"` and `"tags"`
for the concept, collect the node ids, then grep those ids in `"edges"` for the one-hop
neighbourhood. That answers most questions without reading a single source file.
